title: Pages — the shell, round 3: how an open page is framed

steps.path: Any open page, shown here with the week planner
steps.headline: Which frame should an open page sit in?

variants.label: Frameless
variants.summary: No bar at all. The page fills the window; a small Back pill floats top-left and a ⋯ pill top-right holds pin, edit and all pages. Most room for the page; the page's own title does the naming.
variants.risk: A page with a busy top edge has two pills sitting on it, and there is nothing that says where you are.

variants.label: Side panel
variants.summary: A panel on the left: Back to chat, the page's name, your pinned pages to switch between, All pages, and the page actions tucked at the bottom. The page fills the rest.
variants.risk: The panel costs 240 px of width on every page, even ones with nothing to switch to; on a phone it would have to collapse.

variants.label: In the app frame
variants.summary: The page takes the pane the chat normally fills, under the app's own top bar, so the Pages button and pinned buttons stay where they always are. A Chat pill returns you; ⋯ holds the actions.
variants.risk: The composer and status bar are hidden while a page is open, and the rounded pane wastes a little space at the edges.

variants.label: Slim bar
variants.summary: A thin bar: Back, the page's icon and name, and a ⋯ on the right. The Pin and Edit chips from rounds 1 and 2 are gone; they live in the ⋯ menu.
variants.risk: Still a bar above every page, which is the thing you said you may not want.

steps.path: The ⋯ at the top-right of an open page
steps.headline: Pin, Edit in chat and All pages move behind one ⋯ menu, whichever frame you pick.
steps.changed: The Pin and Edit chips are gone from the page's edge. One small ⋯ opens a menu with the three actions, in the same style as the ||| menu at phone width.
steps.notice: The page's top edge is quieter. The actions are one click further away.
steps.risk: Someone who never opens ⋯ may not find pinning from inside a page; the library's card pin still works.
